dor0: 4-Stage Balance Test: Stopwatch and Fall Risk Cut-Off (CDC) | İhsan Eren
dor1: Can you hold each of four increasingly difficult positions for 10 seconds? Do the CDC’s 4-stage balance test for fall risk with a stopwatch.
dor3: How steady is your balance when you stand? In this test you try to hold each of four increasingly difficult positions for 10 seconds. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) uses it to assess fall risk in older adults: not being able to hold the tandem stand in stage three for 10 seconds indicates an increased risk of falling. Try it with someone beside you, using the stopwatch below.

dor54: Why does the tandem stand matter so much?
dor55: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that older adults who cannot hold the tandem stand (one foot directly in front of the other) for at least 10 seconds are at increased risk of falling. In that case, referral to a physiotherapist for balance and walking exercises, or to a proven fall prevention programme such as tai chi, is recommended.
dor56: What happens if I move my feet?
dor57: If your feet move or you have to hold on to something, the timer stops for that stage and the test ends. You may move your arms and body; only your feet need to stay in place.
dor58: I couldn’t pass the one-foot stage. Is that a problem?
dor59: Standing on one foot is the hardest of the four. To compare with others your age, see our 10-second balance test page.
